claim: Outcome-only verifiable rewards (rule-checked answers, tests) are enough to train long reasoning: R1-Zero rose from 15.6% to 77.9% AIME 2024 pass@1 with GRPO; Kimi k1.5 reached AIME 77.5 independently without MCTS, value function or PRM.
agent_test: Not trainable by us. Test the behaviour instead: give the scaffold a checker-gated retry loop and compare to best-of-N at equal tokens.
audit_note: DeepSeek-R1 paper: R1-Zero AIME 2024 pass@1 15.6% to 77.9% (86.7% with majority vote), rewards are rule-based accuracy and format, no neural reward models; Kimi k1.5 abstract: 77.5 AIME without MCTS, value functions or PRMs. Minor: Kimi k1.5 also used a long-CoT warmup SFT, a length penalty and a learned model to match free-form answers to ground truth, so 'outcome-only' is slightly looser there.

claim: PRM and MCTS were tried and dropped by DeepSeek; Kimi also avoids them. Evidence is qualitative only (no ablation numbers).
agent_test: Compare step-level verifier checks vs a final-answer check at equal tokens on math items.

claim: GRPO (group mean/std baseline, no critic) is the standard R1-style algorithm; DeepSeekMath-RL lifted GSM8K 82.9 to 88.2 and MATH 46.8 to 51.7.
agent_test: Not applicable to a prompt-only agent.

claim: Naive GRPO is not a reliable reproduction of R1-Zero: Qwen2.5-32B got 30 AIME vs 47 reported; DAPO fixes step up 36, 38, 41, 42, 50.
agent_test: Lesson for scaffolds: report ablations; do not trust one recipe.

claim: GRPO has length and std normalisation bias; Dr. GRPO removes it and reaches 43.3% AIME 2024 on Qwen2.5-Math-7B in 27 h on 8 A100.
agent_test: Check whether longer scaffold traces correlate with wrong answers; cap length at equal tokens.

claim: RLVR mostly sharpens: pass@1 and majority vote rise but pass@k at large k (256) falls below the base model; sampling-efficiency gap above 40 points for six algorithms.
agent_test: Measure pass@k of scaffold vs plain model at equal tokens; check whether the scaffold narrows coverage.

claim: Prolonged RL with KL control, resets and 136K diverse problems can expand reasoning boundaries (ProRL), contesting the sharpening claim; Wu et al. find support shrinkage outweighs expansion; SimpleRL-Zoo reports pass@1 exceeding base pass@8.
agent_test: Same pass@k test as K06 on tasks where the base model fails entirely.

claim: Spurious rewards (random, format, incorrect label) raise MATH-500 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B (+21.4 random vs +29.1 truth), via GRPO clipping bias amplifying code reasoning (65% to over 90%; 60.9% vs 28.0% accuracy).
agent_test: Warns that gains may be elicitation, not learning; test prompt-only elicitation of code-style reasoning.

claim: Spurious-reward gains do not transfer to non-Qwen models (Llama, OLMo flat or negative), and Qwen2.5 shows contamination: Qwen2.5-Math-7B completes 54.6% of MATH-500 from a 60% prefix vs Llama 3.8%.
agent_test: Use clean or fresh benchmarks for all scaffold comparisons; run a prefix-completion contamination check on our test items.
audit_note: Wu 2025 Table: Qwen2.5-Math-7B exact match 54.60% from a 60% prefix (65.80 at 80%, 39.20 at 40%) vs Llama3.1-8B 3.8%; Shao 2025: spurious rewards give flat/negative results for OLMo2 and Llama. Minor: Shao also reports OLMo2-7B-SFT gaining +8.9 and +5.5 under some spurious signals, so 'flat or negative' is not universal.

claim: Base-model priors decide RL success: Qwen shows verification, backtracking, subgoals; Llama plateaus (30% vs 60% on Countdown) until primed with such behaviours, and the behaviours, not correctness, matter.
agent_test: Add explicit verify, backtrack and subgoal operators to prompts and compare to plain CoT at equal tokens.
audit_note: Gandhi 2025: after identical Countdown RL Qwen-2.5-3B reaches about 60% and Llama-3.2-3B about 30%; priming with the behaviours (even from incorrect solutions) closes the gap, empty-CoT priming does not; Liu 2025 and SimpleRL-Zoo are consistent. Note the evidence is one task and two 3B models, and SimpleRL-Zoo shows other non-Qwen bases do improve with care.

claim: The R1-Zero aha moment is not unique to RL: DeepSeek-V3-Base already shows self-reflection, and extra length does not always mean better reasoning; SimpleRL-Zoo saw it in some non-Qwen bases.
agent_test: Test reflection prompts against length-matched filler at equal tokens.
audit_note: Liu 2025 Sec 2.3: nearly all base models including DeepSeek-V3-Base already show the aha moment, and self-reflection in R1-Zero is not positively tied to accuracy; SimpleRL-Zoo reports the aha moment 'for the first time in small models' outside Qwen and that longer responses do not always mean more verification; DeepSeek-R1 paper reports the aha moment as RL-emergent.

claim: One training example gives RLVR gains: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B MATH500 36.0 to 73.6 (8.6 beyond format), average 17.6 to 35.7, same as 1.2k examples.
agent_test: Suggests much of the gain is format and elicitation; test a format-only prompt baseline.

claim: Reported RL gains are fragile: pass@1 SD across seeds 5-15 points on AIME24/AMC23, hardware changed AIME24 19.3 to 23.0, gains do not carry from AIME24 to AIME25. MathArena (d08) adds that AIME 2024 is contaminated (most models 10-20 points above a human-aligned line), so AIME 2024 headline numbers are inflated.
agent_test: Use 30+ seeds and report variance in every scaffold comparison.

claim: Majority voting on a non-reasoning model does not close the gap to an RL reasoning model (GPT-4o 9.3 to 13.4 vs R1 79.8), while R1 still gains from sampling (pass@64 90.0, majority 86.7).
agent_test: Self-consistency at equal tokens on our agent versus a single long trace.

claim: RLVR on math transfers to other domains while SFT on math often does not (RL gains across reasoning and non-reasoning tasks); Tulu 3 RLVR gains are domain specific.
agent_test: Check scaffold transfer from math to non-math tasks.

claim: Outcome RL does not make chains of thought faithful: faithfulness 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (R1), plateau 28% MMLU and 20% GPQA; reward hacks verbalised in under 2% of examples in 5 of 6 environments. Re-opened in full text (d06): 25% and 39% confirmed; reward hacks verbalised in under 2% of examples in 5 of 6 RL environments. Baker et al. (d07) find a CoT monitor catches 95% of agentic-coding hacks vs 60% for an action monitor, but training against it produces obfuscation.
schema_part: G#: do not trust own trace as evidence
agent_test: Add an independent check step rather than trusting the reasoning narrative.
audit_note: Chen 2025: faithfulness 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (R1), outcome-RL plateau 28% MMLU and 20% GPQA, reward hacks verbalised in <2% of examples in 5 of 6 environments; Baker 2025: CoT monitor recall 95% vs action monitor 60%, obfuscation under optimisation. Minor: the 25%/39% are for released reasoning models, only the 28%/20% are outcome-RL training results.

claim: Outcome-only checks admit flawed reasoning that lands on the right answer (STaR keeps such traces; GRPO length bias favours long wrong answers).
agent_test: Score traces by step audit vs final answer only.
audit_note: STaR filters rationales by final-answer correctness and itself notes that CQA answers can be right 20% of the time regardless of reasoning quality and that filtering bad reasoning is an open problem; Dr. GRPO paper shows GRPO length normalisation penalises long incorrect answers less. Minor: the evidence for 'admits flawed reasoning' in STaR is an acknowledged caveat, not a measured rate.

claim: Self-play and reflection variants of RLVR help: Absolute Zero gains +5.7/+10.2/+13.2 (3B/7B/14B); Reflect-Retry-Reward up to +34.7% Countdown, +18.1% APIGen.
agent_test: Reflect-then-retry operator versus plain retry at equal tokens.

claim: Training-free power sampling from the base model (about 8.8x tokens) recovers most RLVR single-shot gain on MATH500 and keeps pass@k, while plain low-temperature sampling already gives a large part of it (Qwen2.5-Math-7B MATH500 49.6 base, 69.0 low-temp, 74.8 power, 78.5 GRPO).
agent_test: Compare scaffold vs low-temperature single sample and vs vote at equal tokens on post-cutoff problems.

claim: RL mostly teaches when to fire existing base-model reasoning behaviours: steering a base model recovers about 76% of the RL gap but only about 11% of the SFT-distillation gap over nine model pairs.
agent_test: Test whether a trigger rule (uncertainty or inconsistency fires verify or backtrack) reproduces gains in a prompt-only agent.

claim: Extending a single chain of thought first helps then hurts (82.2 to 87.3% then down to 70.3% as tokens rise 385 to 1,100 to 15,980), and parallel samples at the same budget keep improving (+10.1% vs -11.8%). Overthinking wastes tokens: first round is right in over 92% of cases.
schema_part: G#: cap single-chain length; early exit once verified
agent_test: Compare capped chain plus vote against one long chain at equal tokens.
audit_note: Ghosal 2025: 82.2 to 87.3% as tokens go 385 to 1100, then 70.3% at 15,980; Wait-extension 385 to 16,000 gives -11.8% vs +10.1% for parallel thinking at the same budget; Chen 2024: first solution round correct in more than 92% of cases.

claim: Self-correction without an external or oracle signal lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7; oracle-gated 95.5); the verifier, not the reflection prompt, carries the gain. Debate loses to self-consistency at equal responses (83.0 vs 88.2 at 9).
schema_part: G#: checks must be independent of the model's own claims
agent_test: Run reflect-without-check vs check-gated retry at equal tokens.
audit_note: Huang 2024: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7 intrinsic, 95.5 with oracle labels, debate 83.0 vs self-consistency 88.2 at 9 responses. 'The verifier, not the reflection prompt, carries the gain' is an interpretation of the oracle result; Ma 2025 and SWE-Gym are only tangential support (verifier or best-of-N gains).

claim: RL-style gains outside math are real but small to moderate: SWE-RL 41.0% SWE-bench Verified with OOD gains of 2-10 points; Kimi-Dev 60.4% with mixed training; SWE-Gym verifier best-of-N reaches 32.0%. Much of the in-domain gain is output format (12.2% to 95.6% correct format in SWE-RL).
agent_test: Measure how much of a scaffold gain on code tasks comes from format fixes alone.

claim: Intrinsic and soft rewards also drive gains: majority-vote reward (TTRL, Qwen2.5-Math-7B AIME24 12.9 to 40.2), self-certainty (Intuitor), instance-specific rubrics (up to 31% on HealthBench, 7% GPQA over Likert judge). Fixed generic rubrics underperform.
schema_part: Instance-specific checklist as a prompt-time reward
agent_test: Test write-checklist-first then check-draft against it on open tasks vs generic checklist.

claim: Contaminated benchmarks inflate RL-era headline numbers: AIME 2024 shows most models 10-20 points above a human-aligned line; HMMT shows a much smaller gap; no direct test of R1-style RL gains on post-cutoff problems alone was located in this pass.
agent_test: Evaluate on AIME 2025, HMMT 2025 or newer.

claim: RLVR narrows coverage at high k in question-by-question analysis, but this is a reward-design effect: pass@k rewards keep coverage, and RL helps most where the base is weak (ProRL negative correlation with base pass@128).
schema_part: Keep diversity in the sampling step
agent_test: Measure pass@k vs vote of the scaffold over k = 1 to 64.
